FROZEN_LF.txt - UNT batch 25, SEAT LF: THE WALK RULER ON THE LINKS THAT CAN STILL FLIP. ONE MODEL FAMILY (Fable 5.2, claude-fable-5-2).
Written before any code of this seat ran (only file-reading one-liners, a numpy import check (absent under -I) and my note INSIGHT_LF_1 came first).
Brief sha256 57bf144406233d323e120f9fac4c9fdb113f3fcf5edf31aa746ab8eba60775c3 (verified). Stance: convinced UNT's core is right, not that its rules are complete.
Read before this freeze (results I did not compute): batch-18 chair (selected fields), B18 seat SX (protocol_as_run, main_result, verdict, inputs, premises, part of its frozen text),
B18 seat IHY idea IHY-01 and its check, B21 seat LK33 (definitions, main result, verdict, inputs, question) and its two notes, B21 brief (part), B18 brief, coordinator 0277,
PD-20, PD-25, PD-30, PD-33, PD-39 records, batch-11 chair next_tests guards, rule text l.343-353, 398-413, 420-427, 595-601 as text. No batch-25 note of another seat existed yet.

=== 1. DEFINITIONS (none chosen for the principal) ===
GRAPH, START, BIRTH, CUT RULE as SX's protocol on file (my own code): 1024-site diamond torus (8 cells per axis), 4-regular bipartite; owner g with neighbours o1..o4;
 cut = (g,oj) plus (xi,oi) for i != j, xi a neighbour of oi other than g, the three xi distinct; twin T joins o1..o4; heir H joins g and the three xi; bits copied;
 guard: exactly two of the four cut links ON; candidates = guard-passing cuts with the largest tight3 on offer (pairs among the xi sharing a neighbour); ties uniform; fallback counted;
 no second cut criterion.
BODY P30 (the principal's reading: two carriers, any unfired site): every start site written, two-ON, orderly (bond directions 0 and 1 ON) made slightly warm by 4 flips of
 closed alternating ON/OFF cycles found by a seeded alternating walk; no start carriers; 8 seeded loaded start sites. Growth points attempt a Birth at rate 1; the right passes
 to the heir (PD-06/07A), who may fire unwritten (PD-18); each newborn is written at rate w (blocked while a carrier sits on it), releasing one carrier on its site; carriers
 hop along ON links at h = 10 per link to an empty site; a carrier arriving by a hop at a site that is unfired, not loaded and has a guard-passing cut on offer is used up there
 (PD-17, PD-30); the second used-up carrier makes it a growth point (PD-25). No flips, no undo (PD-24 not exercised; PD-29 holds trivially). Classical stochastic stand-in.
 RUNS: w = 1, seeds 25201 and 25202, to 64x (65,536 sites); w = 0.1, seed 25203, to 64x if the ledger allows. Marks = Birth index (PD-13 mark read as event time, PD-20).
LOCK = "these links stop shifting" (LK33's reading A): locked links are REMOVED from the live graph the pull lives on; growth itself is not changed (no cut-lock run;
 a cut-lock would be LK33's reading B - not run here, said openly). The LIVE (unlocked) graph = the body minus locked links; rulers on its largest connected piece.
LOCK READINGS SCANNED (the bound-versus-unbound split is pending; all are readings; none chosen):
 PAIR(p): bound piece = one Birth's newborn pair with both newborns written (BR-BOTH); a seeded uniform share p of such pairs is called bound; locked = every link at a
   bound site (INC). p in {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5}. "Lock share" = locked links / all links, reported for every point.
 PAIR-INT(p), p in {0.5, 1.0}: locked = links with both ends bound. HEIR(1.0): bound = every written heir, INC (expected to shatter the graph).
 RAND(s): the same NUMBER of links as PAIR(0.1) and PAIR(0.3) removed uniformly at random (dilution control: pieces versus mere thinning).
 AGE readings (the "still past"; NOT what PD-33 says - PD-33 lets only small bound pieces lock - run as the contrast and as the two PD-20 SLICE READINGS):
   W1(q) = live links have BOTH ends among the newest share q of events (window, own links); W2(q) = a two-layer window: live links have AT LEAST ONE end among the
   newest share q. q in {1/2, 1/4, 1/8}.
 RING (the native "can it flip without making charge" reading; LK33's LA1): live = links lying on at least one closed 4- or 6-ring whose links alternate ON/OFF.
RULERS (both, on every graph): WALK: simple random walk on the largest connected piece, mean return probability at even times from K = 3 seeded +-1 vectors through
 S = D^-1/2 A D^-1/2; local slopes ds(tau) = -2 log2(P(2 tau)/P(tau)) at tau = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 (128 on whole bodies and controls if time allows); floor flag when
 P(2 tau) < 20 x 2/n. WALK READING = mean of the unflagged ds(16) and ds(32); "plateau" if they differ by under 0.3. LABEL as on file: 16 seeded centres;
 rho = mean eccentricity / (2 (n/2)^(1/3)); ball ratios to the infinite diamond for radii 2..floor((n/2)^(1/3)); 3D-LIKE iff 0.67 <= rho <= 1.5 and all ratios in [0.5, 2];
 else OTHER. Ball slope log2(B(2r)/B(r)) at r = 2, 4, 8 where B(2r) <= n/8.
POINT-SOURCE FALL-OFF: phi solves (D - A) phi = delta_source - 1/n on the largest live piece (conjugate gradients, own code). F(r) = mean phi on the shell at live-graph
 distance r minus mean phi on the shell at 2r (averaged over sources); beta(r) = -log2(F(2r)/F(r)) for r = 2, 3, 4. A pure 1/r reads 1, a log reads 0, 1/r^2 reads 2.
 A beta(r) is FLAGGED (not counted) when the ball of radius 4r holds more than half the piece (saturation mimics a fast fall-off). "NEAR 1/r" = unflagged beta in
 [0.8, 1.25] at two neighbouring r. Sources: 2 to 4 seeded per graph.
COMMON STILL-INTERIOR MEASURE (M4): per doubling, the share of links between two sites that existed at the doubling's start which are cut during it, by depth (graph
 distance of the nearer end from the nearest growth point at the doubling's start).
CONTROLS (known answers): diamond torus 65,536; square sheet 256 x 256; random four-link bipartite graph 65,536 (tree-like); TOY HISTORY (my own, 4-regular, bipartite,
 links join only successive layers; event (p,t) joins (p,t+1) and (p+e_(t mod 3),t+1)): whole 16^3 x 24 (periodic in t) and LIVE SLAB = the newest 4 layers only,
 on 16^3 x 4 (same instance) and 26^3 x 4 (the slab of a wider history; its whole is too large to run - said openly).
REDUCTION LADDER if the 30-minute compute cap binds (each use reported): (1) fall-off sources 4 -> 2; (2) fall-off on seed 25201 and controls only, on a subset
 (whole, PAIR 0.02/0.1/0.3, W2(1/2), W2(1/4), RING); (3) drop RAND; (4) drop the w = 0.1 run; (5) seed 25202 at 32x; (6) K = 2; (7) drop tau = 128.

=== 2. PREDICTIONS (registered probabilities; all UNCHECKED) ===
P1 WHOLE BODY, 64x, both w = 1 seeds: walk reading in 1.7-2.25; label OTHER; ball slope at the largest unsaturated radius above 3.5. P = 0.8.
P2 SMALL LOCKS CHANGE NOTHING: PAIR(p <= 0.05) (lock share under about 0.11): |walk(live) - walk(whole)| < 0.2 in both seeds, largest live piece > 90% of all sites.
   P = 0.85. At PAIR(0.1) (lock share about 0.19) still < 0.2: P = 0.6.
P3 LARGE LOCKS ONLY LOWER THE READING: in no lock reading and at no lock share does the live walk reading exceed the whole body's by 0.2 or more (unflagged): P = 0.8.
   The largest live piece drops below half of the live sites at a PAIR lock share between 0.45 and 0.70 (P = 0.6); near that point the live walk reading is at least
   0.2 BELOW the whole (P = 0.75). RAND at equal lock share reads within 0.2 of PAIR (P = 0.65).
P4 FALL-OFF: whole body beta(r) unflagged values lie in -0.2..0.7 (P = 0.65; risk: small-world saturation); NO lock reading at any share is NEAR 1/r (P = 0.8).
P5 KNOWN-ANSWER CONTROLS: diamond walk 2.8-3.2, beta(2), beta(3) in 0.8-1.25; sheet walk 1.85-2.1, beta in -0.15..0.3; random graph: no plateau, slopes above 4 by
   tau = 16 or floor-flagged, beta above 1.5; toy whole: ds(8) or ds(16) in 3.4-4.4, beta(2) in 1.4-2.4; toy live slab 26^3 x 4: walk reading 2.7-3.3 and beta(3),
   beta(4) in 0.8-1.3 (so the slab reads at least 0.5 below its whole by walk and NEAR 1/r: the test can see a working live graph). P(all controls in band) = 0.5;
   P(the slab control in band on both counts) = 0.7.
P6 AGE / SLICE READINGS: W1(q) falls apart at every q (largest piece under 5% of its sites; P = 0.8). W2(1/2) holds together (largest piece above 80% of its sites;
   P = 0.7); no W1 or W2 reading has a walk reading in 2.7-3.3 with a 3D-LIKE label (P = 0.9).
P7 RING: 0.60-0.88 of links lie on an alternating 4- or 6-ring (P = 0.65); the RING live graph's walk reading does not exceed the whole's by 0.2 (P = 0.8).
P8 M4: links within depth 0-2 of a growth point are cut at 0.2-0.6 per doubling; the share falls with depth (P = 0.7).
P9 w = 0.1 run: same verdicts as w = 1 (walk reading within 0.3 of the w = 1 bodies; P2-P4 hold) (P = 0.7).
REASONING REGISTERED (hand, RECALLED physics UNVERIFIED): Rayleigh monotonicity - removing links cannot turn a walk that always returns into one that escapes; small pieces
 are a rough isometry. So a body that walks about 2 cannot give a live graph with a 1/r pull by any locking; only a body that walks above 2 as a whole can (the toy).

=== 3. THE KILL CHECK (the spec's words) ===
"The unlocked part reads within 0.2 of the whole body by walk at every lock share (locking small pieces changes nothing), and no lock share gives a point-source
 fall-off near 1/r."
 K-a = every scanned lock point (PAIR, PAIR-INT, HEIR, and separately the AGE and RING readings) with unflagged readings has |walk(live) - walk(whole)| < 0.2.
 K-b = no scanned point is NEAR 1/r (definition above).
 KILL MET (literal) iff K-a and K-b. I ALSO register a second, separate label so that a miss of K-a in the WRONG direction is not sold as survival:
 "KILLED IN DIRECTION" iff K-b holds and every point failing K-a reads LOWER than the whole (locks only lower the reading; nothing moves toward 3).
 THE IDEA HOLDS only if some lock point has a live walk reading at least 0.2 ABOVE the whole and moving toward 3, or is NEAR 1/r, in both seeds.
 Registered: P(K-b holds) = 0.8; P(K-a holds literally at every share, AGE and RING included) = 0.15; P(K-a holds for PAIR(p <= 0.05)) = 0.85;
 P(literal kill or killed in direction) = 0.78; P(the idea holds on these bodies) = 0.04.
What each outcome teaches: if killed, hydrogen's target moves from "which links lock" to "what makes the whole grown body walk above 2" (the toy slab shows the working case).

premises.claim: Cut census: a root witnesses a matching of its four opposite neighbours to four distinct same-side sites, itself included.
Forward image: each cut link (u,v) becomes (u,slot.b) and (slot.a,v) with the same bit; newborns blank.
Guard: a cut is offered only if exactly two of its four links are ON.
Flips: EVERY link may flip, with no dependence on age (so natively the live graph is the whole body).
PD-33: only small bound pieces may lock; the space between keeps its links shifting.
PD-20: one site is one record-event.
PD-30 any unfired site; PD-25 two carriers per new growth point.
PD-39: geometry graded both ways, 'space now' first.
Bound versus unbound: 'stable' and 'lasting' apply to bound records; most records are unbound.
The seat spec, kill condition and common guards.
IHY-01 and its check: the pull lives on the links that can flip; a live four-reading history gives no atom; a live slab reads near 1/r.
The growth protocol, both rulers, slice readings and M4 as run on file (my code re-implements the description, not the script).
LK33: bound piece = one written newborn pair; lock readings A (stop shifting) and B (cut-lock); grown flippable rings in about 1000-2100 pieces.

method.python: /usr/bin/python3 -I, pure Python, own code only (lf_core_v1.py, lf_run_v1/v2/v3.py); no network; no script found on disk was run; no target, core or adapter execution; no diagonalisation; no held-out, blind or protected set opened.
method.body: The principal's reading (two carriers, any unfired site), exactly as defined in the frozen file section 1; seeds 25201 and 25202 (w = 1) and 25203 (w = 0.1) to 64x (65,536 sites); seed 25201 regrown to 256x (262,144 sites; identical random stream, so it extends the same body).
method.lock: Applied after growth: locked links are removed from the live graph; rulers on the largest connected live piece. 21 frozen lock points per 64x body (+2 post hoc points on the w = 1 seeds, 5 points at 256x). Growth is not changed by locks (no cut-lock run).
method.rulers: WALK by stochastic trace (3 seeded +-1 vectors, all sources at once), local slopes at tau 4..64 (128 on whole bodies and controls, 256 once), reading = mean of the unflagged slopes at tau 16 and 32. LABEL as on file (16 centres, rho, ball ratios to the infinite diamond from my own coordinate count). Ball slopes. POINT-SOURCE FALL-OFF by conjugate gradients with a uniform background and shell differences (1 = 1/r, 0 = log, 2 = 1/r^2).
method.slice_readings: Two, neither chosen: W1 (links with both ends among the newest share q of events) and W2 (a two-layer window: links with at least one end among the newest share q), q = 1/2, 1/4, 1/8. Bulk-distance labels were NOT used.
method.controls: diamond torus 65,536; square sheet 65,536; random four-link bipartite graph 65,536; toy history whole 16^3 x 24 = 98,304; toy live slab 16^3 x 4 and 26^3 x 4.
reductions_said_openly: fall-off run at every point with 2 sources only on seed 25201 (4 on whole bodies and controls); on seeds 25202 and 25203 on the frozen subset only (ladder steps 1-2)
256x: fall-off on the whole body only, 2 sources (addendum 2)
no cut-lock (reading B) body was grown
PD-32 relaxation and the undo are not in the body (seat TU's subject)
the toy history's whole is measured on 16^3 x 24 only; the 26^3 slab's own whole was too large to run
old-pair stretch not measured (not in this seat's spec); M4 reported as the common still-interior measure

results.headline_negative: NEGATIVE, stated first. (1) No lock reading at any lock share reads above the whole body by walk: over 56 lock points the largest change upward is +0.057 (ruler noise); 29 points read at least 0.2 BELOW the whole. (2) No point is near 1/r: 0 of 29 converged fall-off points (the same with or without the extra addendum-A3 clause). The whole bodies' own fall-off reads about -0.3 (the pull does not fall with distance). (3) Nothing reads near 3 on the walk ruler anywhere on a grown body (whole 1.70-1.86; highest live reading 1.89).

whole_256x_one_more_octave.note: The local slope creeps up with the time scale: 1.85, 1.89, 1.96, 2.05, 2.11 at tau 16..256 (addendum 3: predicted 2.03-2.20; met). No plateau; no sign of 2.67 or 3.

small_locks.statement: PAIR locks, w = 1: within 0.2 of the whole up to lock share 0.20 (largest change -0.15; largest locked cluster at most 1.1% of locked links: small separate pieces); at lock share 0.29 the pieces are still separate (largest cluster 1.3-3.3%) but the walk is already 0.21-0.28 lower. w = 0.1: within 0.2 up to lock share 0.10 (-0.17 there); at lock share 0.16 it is 0.27 lower though the pieces are still small (largest cluster 1.9%). So 'small pieces change nothing' holds only while they are also SPARSE (a tenth to a fifth of all links).

results.break_up: The largest live piece holds 95-96% of live sites at lock share 0.46-0.55 and 22-28% at 0.63, 7% at 0.77 (w = 1). The LOCKED links join into one web between lock share 0.29 (largest cluster 1-3%) and 0.46 (43-82%).
results.pieces_versus_thinning: Removing the same number of links at random lowers the walk by 0.03-0.10 at lock share 0.29 (pair locks: 0.21-0.28) and leaves 99% of sites in one piece: a locked pair deletes whole sites and the body has few spare routes around them.

slice_readings_PD20.W1: falls apart at every q in every body: largest piece 0.2-0.5% of its sites; rulers not run (under 200 sites).
slice_readings_PD20.W2: w = 1: the newest-half two-layer window holds together (91% of all sites, 93-96% of its own) and walks 1.34-1.36, label OTHER (rho 1.9-3.4), ball slopes 1.6-2.6; at q = 1/4 it shatters (1-3%). w = 0.1: shatters already at q = 1/2 (4%).

results.native_flip_reading_RING: 78% of links lie on an alternating 4- or 6-ring, but the graph of those links is dust: largest piece 0.5-1.4% of sites, walk about 0.95, label OTHER.
results.froth_reading: Links with an unwritten end: largest piece 9-19% of all sites at w = 1 (7% at 256x), 42% at w = 0.1; walk 1.2-1.4; label OTHER. Both ends unwritten: dust at w = 1, 2% at w = 0.1.
results.rule_of_thumb_checked: fall-off exponent (distance in links) = ball slope x (1 - 2/walk): diamond 0.93 (seen 0.89-0.93 at r 3-4), slab 26^3 1.04 (0.94-0.99), toy whole 1.82 (1.85 at r 4), sheet 0 (0.0), grown body 3.7 x (1 - 2/1.86) = -0.28 (seen -0.3 on average, noisy). POST HOC consistency check, PROPOSED, no credit.
results.M4_common_still_interior_measure: Old-link cut share per doubling by depth from the nearest growth point (last doubling to 64x): w = 1: depth 0 0.57-0.58, depth 1 0.47-0.48, depth 2 0.25-0.26, depth 3 0.03-0.04, depth >= 4 0.00 (but under 2% of old links lie deeper than 2); w = 0.1: 0.63, 0.51, 0.29, 0.20, 0.08, then 0. Full table per doubling in tables.
results.noise: Walk ruler: the same 256x body read with different random vectors gives 1.853/1.887 against 1.83/1.88 at tau 16/32 (about 0.02); a regrown body reproduces to the digit; body to body 1.83-1.86. what_it_teaches: Locks can only take routes away, so the hydrogen target cannot be reached by choosing what locks: the WHOLE grown body has to walk above 2 first (the working example is a true history with a live slab). With distance counted in links the pull falls as r^-(ball slope x (1 - 2/walk)), so the named target is a pair of numbers, not 'walk 3' alone. The grown body's walk slope creeps upward with scale (2.11 at tau 256): the cheapest next test is whether that creep continues at 1024x and beyond. At slow writing the body is lobes joined only through written-written links - lineage pieces exist (compare HM_2).

questions_for_principal.question: When a small bound piece locks, do its links simply drop out of the web that carries the electric pull, or does the piece still pass the pull through as one solid lump?
options: (A) its links drop out of the web [RECOMMENDED - marked recommendation only, NOT chosen]
(B) it passes the pull through as a solid lump
(C) leave open until a grown body walks above 2
questions_for_principal.evidence: Tested under (A): small pieces change nothing up to a tenth to a fifth of all links locked, and more locking only hurts. Under (B) small pieces should also change nothing (by hand, not run). Either way the answer does not rescue hydrogen on today's bodies.

plain_summary: I asked whether locking small pieces of a grown network leaves a 'live' part that reads three-dimensional and gives a pull falling as one over distance, as an atom needs. It does not. On three networks grown by the carrier rule (to 64 times the start, one to 256 times) the whole network walks about 1.85 and its pull does not fall with distance at all. Locking up to a tenth of the links in small pieces changes the reading by under 0.2; locking more only lowers it, and past about 60 percent the live part falls apart. No reading ever rose above the whole. A toy history with a live slab, the known answer, read 3.2 with a one-over-distance pull, so the test can see success. Lesson: the whole network must walk above 2 before any lock can help. One model family; unchecked; no card moved.
